questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to be elected to the British Parliament and take her seat?
questions.fact: Markievicz was elected first but refused to take her seat as a matter of Irish republican principle.

questions.prompt: Which planet has a moon called Triton that orbits backwards?
questions.fact: The reversed orbit suggests it was captured rather than formed there, and it is slowly spiralling inward.

questions.prompt: Which country hosted the first Commonwealth Games in 1930?
questions.fact: They were called the British Empire Games then, and the name has changed three times since.

questions.prompt: Which musician released the album Born to Run?
questions.fact: He appeared on the covers of Time and Newsweek in the same week, which almost nobody had done.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between Cuba and Mexico?
questions.fact: Its loop current drives the Gulf Stream, which keeps north-western Europe far warmer than its latitude suggests.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the novel Sense and Sensibility?
questions.fact: It was published anonymously, credited only to a lady, and she paid the printing costs herself.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a program's set of instructions in human-readable form?
questions.fact: Some of it is legally protected as literary work, which is why software licences read like publishing contracts.
